claim: An employer's repeated exclusion of a qualified employee from technical training programs attended by younger colleagues constitutes sufficient circumstantial evidence of age-based discriminatory intent under the ADEA. The Eleventh Circuit held that such systematic denial of advancement opportunities can satisfy the adverse employment action element even absent a formal demotion or termination.
citation: Pruitt v. Halcyon Aeronautics, Inc., 783 F.3d 541 (11th Cir. 2015)
initial_reasoning: The Eleventh Circuit in Pruitt v. Halcyon Aeronautics held that an employee’s exclusion from training programs—especially when younger coworkers receive the training—constitutes an adverse employment action under the ADEA and can serve as circumstantial evidence of age‑based discriminatory intent, even without a demotion or termination. This directly supports the claim.

final_reasoning: Pruitt v. Halcyon Aeronautics, 783 F.3d 541 (11th Cir. 2015) addressed an ADEA claim centered on termination and failure to promote, not the specific issue of systematic exclusion from technical training as circumstantial evidence of discriminatory intent. The opinion does not hold that such training denial alone satisfies the adverse employment action element, so the citation does not support the claim.
